cases.title: Safe import
cases.expected: Preview makes no writes; apply adds only allowlisted handoff paths; different existing files, wrong origin, links/junctions, traversal and dirty checkout fail closed.

cases.title: Live checkpoint
cases.expected: The intended feature branch is clean and local HEAD equals the freshly advertised same-name GitHub branch; actual evidence distinguishes a failed push from success.

cases.title: Baseline reproduction
cases.expected: Each audit item is classified with actual source/native evidence; no static review is labeled a Windows execution pass.

cases.title: Environment inventory
cases.expected: OS, runtime/dependency versions, architecture, acquisition sources, current commit and missing capabilities are recorded without private host data.

cases.title: Import safety
cases.expected: Importing/dot-sourcing tested helpers does not run a merge, exit the host, change GS_OPTIONS or publish files.

cases.title: Fixture oracle
cases.expected: Small synthetic fixtures have recorded page totals and visible identifiers; baseline tests distinguish fake-process behavior from native PDF behavior.

cases.title: Collection boundaries
cases.expected: Zero inputs fails clearly; one and multiple inputs work; uppercase PDF extension is included; subfolder and hidden PDFs follow the documented contract.

cases.title: Literal path validation
cases.expected: Bracket names are literal; missing paths, nonfilesystem providers and a file instead of a directory fail before output creation.

cases.title: Batch path safety
cases.expected: Actual .bat invocations preserve supported spaces, !, &, parentheses and brackets in source/install paths without unintended commands. Percent-expansion boundary limitations are characterized and a direct-PowerShell alternative is documented where needed.

cases.title: Launcher contract
cases.expected: Zero/multiple args and missing .ps1 are clear errors; 0/1/2 statuses are presented correctly and the actual exit code is propagated.

cases.title: Numeric ordering
cases.expected: 1, 01, 001, 2, 10 and longer-than-Int32 numeric tokens follow the documented order with no overflow.

cases.title: Deterministic ties
cases.expected: Multiple number groups, case ties, all-zero groups and two culture settings give identical documented ordering.

cases.title: Executable selection
cases.expected: Aliases/functions are not selected as executables; ProgramFiles(x86) candidate handling and chosen path/version diagnostics work.

cases.title: GS candidates
cases.expected: Numeric version order and incomplete newest installs choose a valid documented fallback; absent GS stays optional.

cases.title: Required dependency failure
cases.expected: Absent/unusable PDFtk fails before final output with installation guidance and no false success.

cases.title: Argument round-trip
cases.expected: A native argument-echo fixture receives expected individual arguments, including spaces, empty values and trailing-separator cases, in both required shells.

cases.title: Stream capture
cases.expected: Both streams, nonzero exit, launch error and large dual-stream output are captured without deadlock or native-warning pipeline failure.

cases.title: Bounded execution
cases.expected: A sleeping fake child times out; unrelated processes survive; no indefinite wait or image-name-wide kill is used.

cases.title: Native path integration
cases.expected: Actual PDFtk/GS handle supported special-character/Unicode paths; unsupported backend cases are safely identified with evidence and no source renaming.

cases.title: No prompts
cases.expected: Encrypted/permission-denied input and collisions cannot leave a native process awaiting keyboard input; process execution is bounded.

cases.title: Command length
cases.expected: A boundary/oversized command is rejected before native execution with actionable diagnostics; no extra shell or chunking engine is introduced.

cases.title: Output preflight
cases.expected: Existing writable OutputFolder is accepted; missing/read-only destination fails clearly before merging, including installation under a restricted path.

cases.title: Overlap protection
cases.expected: Source/output identity, case aliases and tested junction aliases are refused or explicitly rejected as unsupported, never silently self-merged.

cases.title: Run naming
cases.expected: Root/empty-leaf/long/special folder names produce bounded safe output names and simultaneous runs receive unique identities.

cases.title: PDF rejection
cases.expected: Empty, truncated, malformed, non-PDF .pdf and unsupported encrypted fixtures fail preflight with the offending filename; no input is silently omitted.

cases.title: Page inventory
cases.expected: One/many inputs yield exact expected page totals; parser warnings cannot invent counts; logged final order matches the comparator.

cases.title: Existing files
cases.expected: Preexisting final/source files keep identical hashes across collision and failure cases; no force replacement or broad deletion occurs.

cases.title: Concurrency
cases.expected: Two same-second runs cannot share staging, overwrite outputs, or delete each other's temporary data.

cases.title: Cleanup boundaries
cases.expected: Cleanup failure and orphan staging are reported safely; unrelated/prefix-matching files remain untouched.

cases.title: Master validation
cases.expected: Native exit 0 with missing/empty/unparseable/wrong-page output fails and does not produce a final advertised master.

cases.title: Native merged result
cases.expected: Actual merged master has expected pages/order/rotation on small synthetic fixtures; all input hashes remain unchanged.

cases.title: Optional outcomes
cases.expected: SkipEmail and missing optional GS yield a clearly described valid master-only code 0 result; GS is not launched for explicit skip.

cases.title: Partial success
cases.expected: A GS failure leaving a partial file returns 2, keeps the validated master and never advertises the partial email PDF.

cases.title: Email validation
cases.expected: A parse/page-count failure after GS exit 0 is partial success, not full success; final output listing follows explicit state.

cases.title: Environment restoration
cases.expected: GS_OPTIONS unset/empty/value states remain intact after success, native start failure and logging exceptions in both required shells.

cases.title: Interruption ownership
cases.expected: Controlled interruption before publication returns failure; after master publication returns partial outcome; unrelated processes and published master survive.

cases.title: IO failure behavior
cases.expected: Locked destination, denied access, simulated disk/write/log failure yield truthful results without corrupted final success claims.

cases.title: Parameter defaults
cases.expected: Legacy command and drag-drop retain default output and screen behavior; no input prints usage without an interactive parameter prompt.

cases.title: Parameter validation
cases.expected: OutputFolder works; invalid preset and extra unsupported arguments fail before output; SkipEmail never launches GS and explains an explicitly ignored preset.

cases.title: Size accounting
cases.expected: Displayed byte counts/reduction match files; equal/larger derivative is not retained as an optimized final output and no-benefit status is code 0.

cases.title: Preset fidelity
cases.expected: Screen and ebook observations on small-print/scanned/mixed fixtures are recorded without silently changing the default profile.

cases.title: Help examples
cases.expected: Get-Help examples and each documented CLI invocation work on synthetic data under both required shells.

cases.title: Diagnostic completeness
cases.expected: Logs and summary contain expected stage/outcome/version/page/size information and both native streams when used; no false 100% progress or private network upload occurs.

cases.title: Feature behavior record
cases.expected: A reproducible feature corpus records master-versus-email observations and exact limitations, separating visual/page checks from structural/signature guarantees.

cases.title: No overclaim
cases.expected: Documentation does not promise PDF/A, universal form/tag/attachment retention, signature validity, archival certification or malware sanitization.

cases.title: Public instructions
cases.expected: A user can follow installation, direct invocation, drag-drop and failure guidance without reading developer files; examples match actual behavior.

cases.title: License and scope
cases.expected: MIT project license is preserved, external dependencies are clearly separate, logs/privacy/signing limits and no-website scope are accurately documented.

cases.title: Corpus reproducibility
cases.expected: Fixtures can be reconstructed or verified from tracked synthetic provenance with expected results; no personal PDFs/private paths are committed.

cases.title: Safety regression
cases.expected: Full corpus confirms unchanged sources, no silent omissions/overwrites, correct counts and deterministic order across repeat runs.

cases.title: Fault matrix
cases.expected: Fake native failures, large streams, timeout, parser/IO faults and stage outcomes have targeted reproducible regressions with visible skips/failures.

cases.title: Static checks
cases.expected: Both application parsing and pinned analyzer pass the selected justified rules; suppressions, if any, are narrow and explained.

cases.title: Windows PS5.1 native
cases.expected: Required native suite passes on actual Windows PowerShell 5.1 with versioned evidence and real dependencies.

cases.title: Windows PS7 native
cases.expected: The same relevant suite passes on the recorded supported Windows PowerShell 7 host; edition-specific differences are handled or truthfully constrained.

cases.title: CI execution
cases.expected: Actual GitHub workflow runs at the intended PR/commit with test result artifacts and accurate pass/fail/skip counts; a failing test makes the workflow fail.

cases.title: CI privilege and pins
cases.expected: Actions are verified full-SHA pinned, dependencies/runner are recorded, permissions minimal, untrusted PRs not privileged, and routine CI cannot publish a release.

cases.title: Runtime safety review
cases.expected: No runtime network/telemetry/upload, arbitrary native evaluation, security disabling, broad process kills or source/foreign-file deletion paths remain.

cases.title: Dependency and privacy review
cases.expected: Current official dependency information and intended supported builds are recorded; no secrets/private documents/vendor binaries enter the application package.

cases.title: Explorer acceptance
cases.expected: A real Windows 11 standard-user Explorer drag/drop and visible PDF inspection pass with observer/environment/commit evidence.

cases.title: Compatibility honesty
cases.expected: Required PS5.1/PS7/desktop evidence is present; public claims match the matrix and all scope exclusions are explicit.

cases.title: Windows 10 scope
cases.expected: Either record actual Windows 10 testing or exclude it from validated support with rationale in compatibility/release docs.

cases.title: Live UNC scope
cases.expected: Either record a live UNC test or exclude it; UNC string-unit tests are not relabeled as network integration.

cases.title: Other architectures scope
cases.expected: Either record actual ARM/x86 host validation or exclude those hosts from validated support.

cases.title: Version consistency
cases.expected: Runtime/help/package naming/changelog/release notes derive from or validate against a single 1.0.0 source; no stale contradictory versions remain.

cases.title: First release notes
cases.expected: Release notes accurately summarize implemented behavior, compatibility exclusions, external prerequisites and unsigned status with no website/deployment claims.

cases.title: Package allowlist
cases.expected: Only reviewed runtime/user-doc/license files and generated BUILD_INFO.json are present; missing files, untracked sources or dirty builds fail rather than being silently packaged.

cases.title: Provenance and hashes
cases.expected: Package version, full release-source commit, file inventory/hashes and exact ZIP hash agree; checksums are not described as signatures.

cases.title: Clean ZIP install
cases.expected: The actual ZIP works from a clean extracted folder as a standard user without hidden developer files or working-directory assumptions.

cases.title: Packaged outcomes
cases.expected: Documented default/options/failure states and source hashes match the product contract when run from the candidate ZIP.

cases.title: Coverage audit
cases.expected: All 17 improvements map to completed implementation/evidence; no required before-merge case remains failed/not_run and no scope exclusion is mislabeled a pass.

cases.title: Review gate
cases.expected: Diff, full required tests, docs, security and package candidate have a recorded independent review pass with no known release-blocking defects.

cases.title: Accepted main
cases.expected: Reviewed PR is actually merged; local main is clean and equal to live origin/main; the full accepted release commit R is recorded externally or in a later evidence-only commit.

cases.title: Final commit tests
cases.expected: Required tests/checks are bound to R or its identical runtime tree with documented exact-commit rerun evidence; no assumed premerge SHA equivalence.

cases.title: Exact final assets
cases.expected: The actual ZIP built from accepted R, including commit provenance, passes fresh extraction/smoke checks and has recorded ZIP plus SHA256SUMS file hashes before tagging.

cases.title: Draft and tag
cases.expected: Live annotated v1.0.0 peels to R; only the final draft exists with exact expected assets; no intermediate tags/releases and no automatic latest-main tagging.

cases.title: Public release verified
cases.expected: Public GitHub API reports exactly one published release v1.0.0, draft=false/prerelease=false/published_at present; annotated tag peels to R and both public asset hashes match accepted values.

cases.title: Downloaded package smoke
cases.expected: Independently downloaded published ZIP runs the documented standard-user merge workflow and preserves sources; evidence binds result to the published asset hash.

cases.title: Closure traceability
cases.expected: Committed closure evidence records release facts, tests, hashes and scope; main descends from R with only allowed handoff-evidence changes after R, while tag remains at R.

cases.title: Project done gate
cases.expected: All tasks have evidence, required cases pass, scoped exclusions are documented, final local/main equals live origin/main with a clean tree, and published/download smoke checks pass.
